You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: G0515

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "To deem worthy, consider deserving; passive: to be counted worthy of honor, calling, or punishment."
  Readable gloss: "The Greek verb axioo carries the weight of deliberate evaluation — to look at someone and judge whether they measure up. In the active voice, it means 'to consider worthy' or 'to think fitting,' as when the centurion tells Jesus 'I did not consider myself worthy to come to you' (Luke 7:7) or when Paul's companions refused to consider Mark a worthy travel companion (Acts 15:38). In the passive, it shifts to 'be counted worthy' or 'be deemed deserving,' and here the stakes rise dramatically: the Thessalonians are counted worthy of God's calling (2 Thess 1:11), elders deserve double honor (1 Tim 5:17), Jesus is deemed worthy of greater glory than Moses (Heb 3:3), and — most soberly — apostates are judged deserving of worse punishment (Heb 10:29). Spanish considerar digno and German wuerdig erachten both capture the evaluative force, while French juger digne brings out the judicial overtone."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "to be counted worthy, be deemed deserving (passive/middle)"
    Enriched: To be counted worthy or deemed deserving in the passive or middle voice, expressing a judgment rendered upon the subject by another authority. The four occurrences cluster around God's evaluative verdict: the Thessalonians whom Paul prays God will 'count worthy of his calling' (2 Thess 1:11), elders 'considered worthy of double honor' (1 Tim 5:17), Jesus 'counted worthy of greater glory than Moses...
    Existing Spanish translations: considere-dignos, ha-sido-considerado-digno, sean-considerados-dignos, será-considerado-digno
  Sense 2: "to consider worthy, think fitting (active)"
    Enriched: To consider worthy, think fitting, or deem appropriate in the active voice, where the subject exercises deliberate judgment about someone's worth or suitability. The centurion in Luke 7:7 declares 'I did not consider myself worthy' (ouk emauton exiosa) to approach Jesus. In Acts 15:38 Paul 'did not think it fitting' (exiou) to take Mark. In Acts 28:22 the Roman Jews say 'we consider it worthwhile'...
    Existing Spanish translations: consideraba, consideramos-digno, tuve-por-digno
